components.text: Whether the asserted explanatory virtues reliably discriminate the divine hypothesis from competing explanations.
Whether the asserted explanatory virtues reliably discriminate the divine account from competing explanations.
Whether logical attributes reliably point to the sufficiently specific personal-mind hypothesis asserted.
Whether God may be selected as the best explanation without an adequately complete and compared candidate set.
Whether God can be selected as the best explanation when the candidate set and comparative assessment are incomplete.
Whether the proposed transcendent personal mind is specified sufficiently to receive discriminating support from logical attributes.
Whether the proposed transcendent personal mind is specified enough for logical facts to support it over alternatives.
Whether comparative abductive superiority is warranted absent candidate coverage, likelihood data, and known supernatural causation.
Whether the asserted divine explanation has comparative likelihood support rather than merely filling a natural-explanation gap.
Whether failure of selected impersonal accounts licenses the inference to supernatural personal agency.
Whether logical attributes support a necessary personal mind better than the available alternatives.
Whether logical attributes are better explained by the necessary personal mind proposed in the opening.
Whether necessarily true logical laws require an additional divine ground rather than holding independently.
Whether necessary logical truths require a further divine ground rather than holding independently.
Whether the truth of logical laws depends on a personal mind or divine creative act.
Whether logical truths can remain unexplained and independent of a personal ground.
Whether abstract logical truths can stand independently rather than being grounded in a mind.
Whether the proposed mental ground supplies a coherent explanatory category rather than an empty label.
Whether mathematical and logical truths require a further entity or personal foundation to guarantee them.
Whether logical and mathematical truths need a mental or other ontological ground beyond describing identity relations.
Whether truth such as two plus two equals four requires an additional guaranteeing foundation.
Whether the premises supporting the mind-grounding inference have been demonstrated rather than merely arranged validly.
Whether a formally valid grounding argument supplies good evidence without demonstrated truth of its premises.
Whether asserted explanatory virtues demonstrate the premises needed for the divine conclusion.
Whether deductive implication and abductive support can provide evidence for premises and a sound philosophical argument.
Whether evidence must satisfy direct empirical repeatability rather than broader philosophical warrant.
Whether the premises received evidential support sufficient for soundness rather than formal validity alone.
Whether good evidence must be directly empirical, repeatable, and independently verifiable.
Whether abductive reasoning is admissible evidence despite incomplete empirical access to supernatural causation.
Whether even striking evidence can abductively identify the specific personal God rather than merely support generic theism.
Whether extraordinary evidence can abductively identify the specific personal deity claimed rather than merely support some god hypothesis.
Whether evidence favoring some mind or god establishes the particular personal deity associated with the pro case.
Whether the demanded reliable link is set so strongly that no possible observation could satisfy it.
Whether perpetual naturalistic or brute-fact alternatives prevent any evidence from confirming a divine conclusion.
Whether the demanded evidential link is merely reliable and discriminating or instead requires unattainable incontrovertibility.
Whether allowing unknown or naturalistic alternatives prevents any observation from supporting God.
Whether withholding confirmation from one anomaly amounts to rejecting all evidential support.
Whether merely possible unspecified candidates defeat an otherwise supported abductive comparison.
Whether absent a substantive rival, the possibility of another explanation warrants withholding the abductive conclusion.
Whether merely possible unnamed alternatives defeat an otherwise supported abductive inference.
Whether the con objection supplies substantive comparative defects beyond an unspecified possible alternative.
Whether describing the reliable function of transcendental facts answers the separate meta-level demand for their ground.
Whether describing the reliable operation of transcendental facts answers the separate meta-level question of their ground.
Whether apparent necessity independently resolves the demand for an explanation of that necessity.
Whether God remains evidentially hidden despite an alleged cumulative public disclosure through creation, morality, logic, revelation, and resurrection.

Whether available evidence identifies the Christian God rather than merely some generic deity.
Whether observed nonbelief fits the claimed divine aim and effective mechanism of universal disclosure.
Whether existing revelation fulfills the claimed divine aim that everyone know God exists.
Whether the pro position actually asserts that God intends every person to acquire settled knowledge or conviction.
Whether the relevant divine aim is universal settled knowledge or revelation sufficient to impose an obligation to know.
